item.title: Features
item.description:
Source: https://www.pgbouncer.org/features.html

  • Connection pooling modes with different connection reuse intervals:

    Session pooling
    PgBouncer assigns a server connection to a client for its entire session. The connection returns to the pool when the client disconnects. This mode changes connection assignment least often and supports all PostgreSQL features.
    Transaction pooling
    PgBouncer assigns a server connection only during a transaction. The connection returns to the pool when the transaction ends. Some PostgreSQL session features cannot work in this mode. The application must avoid these features. See the table below.
    Statement pooling
    This mode changes connection assignment most often. It uses transaction pooling but disallows multi-statement transactions. It enforces client autocommit mode and mainly targets PL/Proxy.

  • Low memory use: 2 kB per connection by default. PgBouncer does not need to hold a complete packet at once.

item.title: Configuration: pgbouncer.ini
item.description:
Source: https://www.pgbouncer.org/config.html · 1.26.0 source

Description

The configuration file uses INI format. Section names appear between [ and ]. Lines beginning with ; or # are comments and are ignored. Elsewhere in a line, these characters have no special meaning.

Generic settings

logfile

Specifies the log file. For daemonization (-d), either this or syslog need to be set.

item.title: Usage: pgbouncer command
item.description:
Source: https://www.pgbouncer.org/usage.html · 1.26.0 source

Synopsis 

pgbouncer [-d][-v][-u user] <pgbouncer.ini>
pgbouncer -V|-h

On Windows, the options are:

pgbouncer.exe [-v][-u user] <pgbouncer.ini>
pgbouncer.exe -V|-h

Additional options for setting up a Windows service:

pgbouncer.exe --regservice <pgbouncer.ini>
pgbouncer.exe --unregservice <pgbouncer.ini>

Description

pgbouncer is a PostgreSQL connection pooler. Applications connect to pgbouncer as they would to PostgreSQL. pgbouncer creates a server connection or reuses an existing one.

item.title: PgBouncer compilation and installation
item.description:
Source: https://www.pgbouncer.org/install.html · 1.26.0 source

Building

Build PgBouncer with Autoconf or the newer, experimental Meson build system. Autoconf is currently recommended for production builds and packages. Meson is expected to become the default, and a future release is expected to remove Autoconf. Test Meson and report problems. Compilation requires:

  • Libevent 2.0+
  • pkg-config
  • OpenSSL 1.0.1+ for TLS support
  • a C11-capable C compiler
  • (optional) c-ares as alternative to Libevent’s evdns
  • (optional) LDAP libraries
  • (optional) PAM libraries

The Meson build additionally needs Meson 0.58+ and Ninja; the Autoconf build needs GNU Make 3.81+.

item.title: Changelog
item.description:
Source: https://www.pgbouncer.org/changelog.html · 1.26.0 source

PgBouncer 1.26.x

2026-09-23 - PgBouncer 1.26.0 - “Ignore all previous search_path”

  • Security
    • Fix CVE-2026-19888: PgBouncer before 1.26.0 did not check that the SCRAM client-final-message contained a nonce. An unauthenticated remote attacker could crash PgBouncer by sending a client-final-message without one. This also applies to users that do not exist, because PgBouncer runs a mock SCRAM exchange for those. This bug has existed since SCRAM support was added in PgBouncer 1.11.0.
    • Fix CVE-2026-6668: Before 1.26.0, integer overflow in packet buffer growth could make PgBouncer loop indefinitely. This required a large amount of data in one packet buffer. With default max_packet_size, an unauthenticated client could trigger it. Because PgBouncer is single-threaded, it stopped serving all clients until the process was killed.
    • Fix CVE-2026-6669: Before 1.26.0, PgBouncer accepted an unbounded SCRAM iteration count from servers. A malicious or compromised PostgreSQL server could force unlimited work during one login. This blocked service for all other clients and databases. The iteration count must now be at most 1000000.
  • Features
    • Track all parameters that PostgreSQL reports by default. These include search_path on PostgreSQL 18+ and default_transaction_read_only on PostgreSQL 14+. Previously, SET search_path or SET default_transaction_read_only = true in transaction pooling affected later clients that used the same server connection. (#1580, #1573)
    • Add pool_idle_timeout to remove pools unused for a configured period. This helps when many users connect infrequently and pool counts otherwise grow without limit. The default disables this setting because pool removal also removes its statistics. (#1491)
    • Allow query_wait_timeout to be configured per user and per database. (#1449)
    • Add client_login_count stat to SHOW STATS, which counts successful client logins. This makes it possible to detect clients that churn connections. (#1457)
    • Send PgBouncer-specific ParameterStatus messages at client login: pgbouncer.version, pgbouncer.pool_mode, and pgbouncer.max_prepared_statements. Clients and drivers can use these to detect PgBouncer and adjust their behavior. (#1490)
    • Add login_notify_message setting. When set, its value is sent to clients as a NOTICE message after they log in. This can be used to make it clear to clients that they are connected through PgBouncer instead of directly to PostgreSQL. (#1488)
    • Add support for building PgBouncer with meson, including a Windows build using the UCRT64 environment. Autoconf builds continue to be supported. (#1524, #1426, #1568, #1585, #1602, #1607)
    • Add a logo. (#1609)
  • Changes
    • Remove the deprecated online restart (-R, aka takeover) functionality, together with the SHOW FDS and SUSPEND admin commands that only existed to support it. Use rolling restarts with so_reuseport instead. (#1581)
    • Increase the maximum length of passwords to 65535 bytes, matching libpq. (#1310, #1520)
    • Treat a NULL user name returned by auth_query the same as no rows being returned, instead of treating it as an error. (#1569)
    • Accept SET extra_float_digits on the admin database, which newer PostgreSQL JDBC drivers send during connection setup. (#1550)
    • Allow mkauth.py to write to stdout by passing - as the output file. (#1514)
    • Stop logging noisy errors on unexpected EOF from clients when built against OpenSSL 3. (#1507)
    • Include the underlying system error in TLS error messages when built against OpenSSL 3. (#1492)
    • Require a C11 compiler. (#1417)
    • Log which limit caused a server connection to be evicted. The disconnect reason is now evicted for max_db_connections, evicted for pool_size or evicted for max_user_connections instead of the bare evicted. (#1597)
  • Fixes
    • Fix late COPY messages causing pool exhaustion in transaction pooling mode. This also makes COPY work outside of an explicit transaction in transaction pooling mode. (#1471)
    • Fix LDAP authentication failures with long DNs by increasing the maximum LDAP URL length. (#1497)
    • Fix SCRAM pass-through corruption of cached forced-user credentials. This caused server login failures because the real server rejected the SCRAM proof. (#1612)
    • Fix SCRAM pass-through with stored SCRAM secrets after server reconnection. It failed with “password is SCRAM secret but client authentication did not provide SCRAM keys”. (#1504, bug introduced in 1.25.1)
    • Fix use-after-free crash when a replication client disconnects while its server connection is still logging in. (#1577)
    • Fix idle server eviction for replication clients when the pool is full. Previously, one replication client could evict every idle server instead of one. No eviction occurred when reserve pools or cancel requests made the server count exceed pool_size. (#1597)
    • Fix stalled TLS connections when a packet straddles the packet buffer boundary, for example a SET application_name with a long value. (#1531)
    • Fix prepared statement responses being sent in the wrong order when a batch mixes Parse and Close messages without a Sync in between. (#1555)
    • Fix parameters listed in track_extra_parameters that are not reported by the server causing incorrect behaviour when a client sets them in its startup packet. (#1576)
    • Fix login failures when the server splits its login packets across multiple TCP packets, for example when there is another proxy between PgBouncer and PostgreSQL. (#1446)
    • Fix query_timeout closing connections when no query was in flight. (#1395)
    • Fix sending a duplicate NegotiateProtocolVersion message when no server was available right away. (#1460)
    • Fix pool_size column in SHOW USERS showing a value for users that do not have one configured. (#1489)
    • Fix error message for ENABLE admin command. (#1308)
    • Fix compilation against future OpenSSL versions that make struct asn1_string_st opaque. (#1440)
    • Prevent the compiler from optimizing away the erasure of sensitive cryptographic data from the stack. (#1508)
    • Fix linking of pgbevent.dll with clang on Windows. (#1571)
    • Fix paths of root-level files in the release tarball, which were stored as pgbouncer-X.Y.Z/./configure instead of pgbouncer-X.Y.Z/configure. (#1549)
    • Fix a memory leak when reading track_extra_parameters from the config. (#1510)
    • Fix a memory leak for every startup packet that contained a protocol extension parameter (_pq_. prefix), which could be triggered by unauthenticated clients. (#1540)

PgBouncer 1.25.x

item.title: Frequently Asked Questions
item.description:
Source: https://www.pgbouncer.org/faq.html

How to connect to PgBouncer?

PgBouncer acts as a Postgres server. Configure your client to use the PgBouncer port.

How to load-balance queries between several servers?

PgBouncer supports comma-separated hosts in a database connection string. With load_balance_hosts=round-robin, new server connections use each host in turn. For example:

[databases]
app = host=pg1,pg2 port=5432 dbname=app load_balance_hosts=round-robin

item.title: PgBouncer 1.26.0 Documentation
item.description:
Source: https://www.pgbouncer.org/

This manual is based on PgBouncer 1.26.0, released on 2026-09-23. See the release notes for the changes from earlier versions.

pgbouncer is a PostgreSQL connection pooler. Applications connect to pgbouncer as they would to a PostgreSQL server. pgbouncer creates a server connection or reuses an existing connection.

pgbouncer reduces the performance cost of opening new PostgreSQL connections.

To preserve transaction semantics, pgbouncer supports these connection pooling modes:

  • Session pooling: PgBouncer assigns a server connection to a client for its entire session. When the client disconnects, the connection returns to the pool. This is the default mode and changes connection assignment least often.
  • Transaction pooling: PgBouncer assigns a server connection only during a transaction. When the transaction ends, the connection returns to the pool.
  • Statement pooling: The connection returns to the pool immediately after each query. This mode changes connection assignment most often and does not allow multi-statement transactions.
